Fairfield Island is a residential neighbourhood in the City of Chilliwack, north of Chilliwack Proper, reached by Young Road North, Menzies Road, Hope River Road, Clare Avenue, Bell Road and Ballam Road.

The City plans it together with Chilliwack Proper: Schedule B2 of the 2050 Official Community Plan (Official Community Plan Bylaw 2025, No. 5500) is the Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan.
Cartmell Road is the park road at the north end: Island 22 Regional Park is at 44955 Cartmell Road, on the Fraser River.
Strathcona Road carries the neighbourhood's elementary school, Strathcona Elementary at 46375 Strathcona Road.

The one housing fact the plan frame settles is tenure context: this is a Schedule B2 residential neighbourhood inside the city-wide zoning frame of Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000, with the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) administration the City describes applying to farm parcels on its edges.

Island 22 Regional Park, the area's largest single land use, is a 132-hectare park with an equestrian area, a boat launch, walking trails, an off-leash dog park, a bike skills park and a picnic shelter.

blocks.text: Fairfield Island: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Dike and flood construction rules are the defining buyer rule here: the City's Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519 designates floodplain land and sets flood protection requirements, and its Schedule A floodplain map is where a Fairfield Island parcel is checked.

blocks.text: Fairfield Island: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Island 22 is owned as a City park but run regionally: it is a 132-hectare Fraser Valley Regional District park at 44955 Cartmell Road, and the Island 22 Equestrian Society maintains the equestrian area, including a cross-country field, jumps, riding rings, trails and corrals.
The park connects to a section of the Experience the Fraser Canyon to Coast Trail, so dike-top trail traffic passes the north end of the neighbourhood.

Below-flood-level living space is restricted: the area below the flood construction level in a residential building may be used only for uses such as a utility room, workshop or indoor recreation, and its floor must sit at least 0.3 metres above the crown of the road.

An older home here can be partly outside today's flood rules: the bylaw's elevation requirements do not apply to a renovation or addition that increases the building by less than 25 percent of the floor area that existed when the previous floodplain bylaw was adopted in March 1997.
One cost is specific to the park, not the houses: Island 22's seasonal parking fees run June 29 to October 25, 2026, per the Fraser Valley Regional District fee table in.
Route 53 Fairfield is the island's bus, running between the neighbourhood and Downtown Chilliwack, and it gained added Sunday-evening service on January 4, 2026.
The Canyon to Coast Trail section at Island 22 gives a dike-top walking and cycling link along the Fraser River from the north end of the neighbourhood.

blocks.text: Fairfield Island: risks and due diligence

items.t: Start with the floodplain map: Schedule A of Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519 designates the floodplain areas, and the bylaw's flood construction levels are read off that schedule for the specific parcel.
The bylaw sets a minimum setback of 60 metres from the natural boundary of the Fraser River for buildings requiring floodproofing.

The City warns that its published floodplain elevation figures are estimates: the floodplain elevations map states the figures carry a margin of error of plus or minus 20 centimetres, that flood construction levels inside the dike are rough estimates of an 1894-magnitude flood, and that no one should rely on them alone to estimate or mitigate flood risk.
Riparian parcels fall under Development Permit Area 3, which protects fish habitat and riparian areas, and ALR status for any parcel is checked on the City Webmap before an application.

blocks.text: By the river, north of Chilliwack Proper, Fairfield Island is a residential area. It appeals to acreage, workshop and custom-home buyers.
Fairfield Island home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

39 houses sold in Fairfield Island with a median price of $850,000 (the middle half sold between $792,500 and $957,500), taking a median of 24 days to sell at 97.6% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $377 per square foot, a median year built of 1976 and a median lot of 7,710 square feet.

faq.q: Is Fairfield Island really an island, and what does that mean for a purchase?
faq.a: What matters for a purchase is the dike and floodplain frame, whatever the name. The neighbourhood sits in the Fraser River floodplain area the City regulates under Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519: new building must meet the flood construction level plus 0.6 metres freeboard, setbacks apply from the Fraser River's natural boundary, and a covenant can be registered on title where freeboard is waived.

faq.q: Which elementary school serves a Fairfield Island address?
faq.a: Check the exact address, because School District No. 33 catchments are address-based. The school located in the neighbourhood is Strathcona Elementary at 46375 Strathcona Road, and the other schools named for this side of the city are Little Mountain Elementary at 9900 Carleton Street, A D Rundle Middle School at 45660 Hocking Avenue and Chilliwack Secondary at 46363 Yale Road; no catchment result is confirmed here.

faq.q: Can I build or add a suite on an ALR-edge parcel here?
faq.a: Only through the ALC process where the parcel is in the Agricultural Land Reserve. The City states an Agricultural Land Commission application may be required for a new house, coach house or suite, for placing fill or removing soil, for non-farm uses and for subdivision, and it directs owners to check ALR status on the City Webmap before applying.

faq.q: Is there a bus, or is this a drive-everywhere area?
faq.a: One named bus route serves the island: British Columbia Transit (BC Transit) Route 53 is the Fairfield route, and BC Transit's January 4, 2026 service changes added Sunday-evening service on Route 53 Fairfield along with Routes 51 and 57 Broadway. Everything else — shopping, the hospital, Highway 1 — is off the island, so most trips still start with a car.

faq.q: Can ALR rules affect a Fairfield Island property?
faq.a: They can where a parcel is in the Agricultural Land Reserve: ALR properties are subject to the Agricultural Land Commission Act and regulations, ALC approval may be required before the City can approve related development, and an ALC application may be required for a new house, coach house or suite, fill or soil removal, a non-farm use, or a subdivision or boundary adjustment; check a parcel on the City Webmap.

faq.q: What plan governs building in Fairfield Island?
faq.a: The City's 2050 Official Community Plan, Official Community Plan Bylaw 2025, No. 5500, including the Schedule B2 Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan and the Schedule D development permit areas.

faq.q: What did houses in Fairfield Island sell for?
faq.a: 39 houses sold in Fairfield Island between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $850,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Fairfield Island?
faq.a: The median was 24 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.6% of the last list price (0% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
